answer.reason: The verses tell of Joash's visit to the dying Elisha, his victories over Benhadad, and his defeat of Amaziah of Judah, which go beyond the summary.

clauses.english: smote the ground with arrows three times at Elisha's word, and stayed
clauses.quote: And he smote thrice, and stayed.

clauses.english: beat Benhadad three times and recovered the cities of Israel
clauses.quote: Three times did Joash beat him, and recovered the cities of Israel.

clauses.english: defeated Amaziah king of Judah at Bethshemesh and broke down the wall of Jerusalem
clauses.quote: brake down the wall of Jerusalem from the gate of Ephraim unto the corner gate, four hundred cubits.

doubts: 2KI 13:9 and 14:23 name Jehoahaz's father or Jeroboam son of Joash as context; HOS 1:1 and AMO 1:1 name Jeroboam son of Joash, not this record, and were left out.
2KI 13:14 and 13:16 concern his visit to Elisha, but only the arrow-smiting was given a clause as the single event.
